newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit retains gains after curbs.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit retains gains after curbs.

text.p: 0315 GMT - Malaysian ringgit retains early gains after central Bank Negara announces curbs on swaps by Malaysian banks.
* Ringgit quoted at 2.6078/98 to dollar after sharp spike up in thin Sydney markets.
* Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
* Move seen as part of effort to discourage speculation in ringgit. Further curbs expected by some analysts, including possible imposition of negative interest rates on foreign deposits.
* Ringgit's upside seen capped around 2.5980 for now.
* Thai baht firms on dollar sales by exporters ahead of economic rescue plan, due to be presented to cabinet on Tuesday.
* Market upbeat as Thai economic ministers begin meeting to discuss package of measures between finance minister and International Monetary Fund (IMF).

* Singapore dollar quoted at 1.4650/60 to dollar, tracking movements in ringgit. * Indonesian rupiah underpinned by tighter liquidity. Swaps show upward bias on fears Indonesia will introduce similar curbs to Malaysia.
* Taiwan dollar firm but off opening highs after central bank's intervention on Saturday to stem currency's sharp decline.
* Strong demand for U.S. dollar seen capping Taiwan dollar's upside.

* Philippine peso little changed from opening 29 to dollar level. Seen gaining as banks sell dollars to improve their liquidity after central bank ordered two percentage-point increase in liquidity reserves last week.
* Central bank raises overnight lending rate to 26 percent on Monday from 22 percent due to tightening liquidity.
